assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit: COTE_Y2_02_AYANOKOJI_CHARACTER_PSYCHOLOGY_ETHICS_AND_VOICE.md (125,907 bytes, status canonical, veto false), a specialist synthesis over the frozen Year 1 V2 conclusion, Japanese Y2V01-Y2V12.5, Volume 0 at its mandated position after Y2V08 and the Year 2 guidebook Second List, with Year-3 narrative evidence excluded. Read in full by the evaluator. The Ayanokoji character, ethics, relationship, voice and ordinary-life ledgers, the Y2 deep readings and the active_provisional behavioral reconstruction protocol it routes to are not curated on this subject and were not used. The item's own statement that its evidence supports bounded voice realization is an input, not a conclusion; the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Year-2 states Y2V01 through the Second List boundary (Y2SL), at the item's volume resolution: V01 visibility change and school-life priority; V05 culling; V06 training-wheels succession; V08 voluntary non-optimization and timing jurisdiction over Ichinose; V09.5 inefficient desire, Hiyori invitation, manipulation pleasure and the Kei romance audit; V10 involuntary smile and all-class project; V11 stopping rule; V12 relational sovereignty; V12.5 breakup and class transfer. Year 1 enters only as the item's frozen baseline and claim-transition ledger. His White Room formation and Atsuomi's preference engineering are his own history at every state; only the reader's access to them dates from Volume 0. No Year-3 state.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: A four-layer model (ordinary adolescent, relational, White Room/strategic, environmental-author; section 3) held as simultaneous rather than mask and core, a nonclinical profile table (section 4) and named injury, strength, danger, need and fear (4.1-4.6, 20.1-20.5). The account says what changes his response: stakes (low-stakes scenes default to ordinary response families, 19.2; high stakes to environmental authorship and asymmetric information, section 20 table), the relationship (19.6), what he knows versus his model of the target (19.4), and chronology (section 14). It predicts his overreach: hidden timetables (V08), authored culling (V05), trust used as a control surface (V12), and pleasure in verbal manipulation (V09.5). Not A: the item leaves open whether attachment restrains high-control intervention when stakes are high (17.5 items 1-2) and states that motive weights can be underdetermined (19.5). Not C: the account discriminates by stakes, relationship, knowledge and chronology and states where it stops (19.9).

A volume-by-volume progression table from Y2V01 to Y2SL with function, development and caution per position (section 14), a Year 1 to Year 2 claim-transition ledger (section 2), Volume 0 placed after Y2V08 as retrospective genealogy rather than chronology (0.6, section 15), and the V11/V12 pair as a located pair of states. Not A: Year 1 enters only as summarized baseline, resolution is per volume with no intra-volume splits, and transitions are not page-located. Not C: the state changes are dated by volume and earlier states keep their own boundaries.

Written-Japanese rules: stable オレ across modes (12.1); a sparse, understated spoken register separated from a broad interior register (12.1, 12.8); causal understatement as an invariant (12.5, V07 `オレがしたことは本当に些細なことばかりだ。`); emotion handled analytically before confession (12.6); self-correction as a development marker (12.7); expanding participant speech acts (12.4, V11 `ここから先は、オレの立ち入る領域じゃない。`); and an explicit avoid list (12.12, 19.8). About seven lines are quoted (also V01 `おまえの実力は認めている。だが自分の運命は自分で決める。`, `学校生活を続けることが、今のオレにとって最優先すべきこと`, V04.5 `友人の作り方は、教科書に載せられるものじゃないな`, V11 `利害に関係なく`). Not B: relationship-specific voice is asserted (12.11) but not specified per dyad, and the item lists the address-term crosswalk, frequency distributions and narration-mode classifier as open (12.13). Not D: stable, mode-conditioned constraints with quoted anchors and a public/interior separation.

A recurring, volume-located ordinary layer: grocery shopping, cooking and domestic mess (V01), embodied intimacy, piano and cruise life (V03-V04.5), joining the beginner ski group and falling (V08), fear of a rejected invitation and the yogurt maker bought after he stops his own cost analysis (V09.5), the blank sketchbook (V10), purposeless talk with Horikita (V11), the habitual second rice bowl after the breakup (V12.5). A default rule: without an exam, threat or evidence of a developmental frame, prefer ordinary response families, and an invitation can be an invitation (19.2; 19.7 observe, understated response, allow refusal). Not A: exact topics, jokes and purchases stay open (19.7), and ordinary life outside the school is unsampled. Not C: a stated rule with recurring located instances across many volumes.

Partner-specific defaults and diagnostic tests (sections 9 and 19.6): Kei (attraction, routine, curriculum framing, decisive disclosure failure, current substitutability at V09.5); Horikita (trust in her judgment, consequential disagreement accepted, purposeless conversation, the hidden separation timetable); Ichinose (sincere care, timing jurisdiction at V08, trust weaponized at V12, then model surprise); Sakayanagi (mutual recognition, indirect jurisdiction through her inferred reading of his preference at V12); Hiyori (low-control participant mode, invitations with refusal space); Ryuen (rivalry as self-authentication). Not A: dyad speech forms are open, and how an untested new person is treated is an abstention (19.9). Not C: the response policy changes with the partner, and the changes are located.

First-person narration is treated as evidence with domain-specific reliability (0.2 table: very high for mechanism and tactics, partial for his own motives, not privileged on moral legitimacy). Located inner states: the V09.5 yogurt-maker reversal, fear of rejection, the V09.5 romance self-audit separating romantic behaviors from the expected feeling, the V10 smile read by him after the fact, and the V11 jurisdiction statement. The item also records a focalization trap at V12.5, where an interior near him belongs to Kei (12.9). Not A: his own motives are layered and selectively narrated, and voluntary protective vulnerability is unproven (Y1H-035). Not C: inner states are located, sequenced and tied to conduct.

A six-step environmental-authorship grammar (3.4, 17.1 C) with per-volume instances: procedure and witness redesign against Tsukishiro (V04), the culling branch with admissible criteria and coalition logic (V05), staged agency in the Yagami operation (V07), relational sovereignty (V12); plus calibrated violence (V01 knife wound, V04 Nagumo incapacity, V06 Sakayanagi counter-leverage, 13.4-13.6). It predicts how he hides authorship (causal understatement, 12.5) and names the costs he imposes (externalities, V04). Not A: how he responds after a genuine personal failure is outside the corpus (19.9), and fight mechanics are not analyzed. Not C: the conditions that select indirect over direct coercion are explicit and recur.

Located positions with reasons: mild paternalism through withheld rescue information (V03), protective incapacity with system costs (V04), authored culling with Airi's sincere final request (V05), deniable stage-setting (V07), care with timing jurisdiction (V08), pleasure in manipulation (V09.5), the V11 stopping rule and the V12 relational sovereignty. The item explains why conduct differs: favorable, lower-stakes access cases admit the stopping rule; high-stakes project cases revert to authored choice (8.11-8.12, 17.1 G). It predicts the characteristic failure, superior diagnosis treated as jurisdiction (8.15, 20.3). Not A: whether the stopping rule generalizes to a new high-stakes relation is an abstention (19.9), and early disclosure is open (Y1H-004). Not C: the conditions that change his ethical conduct are stated and located.

The ordinary/comic オレ register is identified and treated as positive evidence (12.2): invitation anxiety, food, shopping, the yogurt maker, skiing, bus etiquette, embarrassment and unfamiliar everyday knowledge. The item warns against a permanently sarcastic register and against making every ordinary joke strategic (12.12). Not B: no comic lines are quoted and no account of his comic mechanics is given. Not D: the register is named, recurs across volumes and is distinguished from strategy.

One canonical synthesis covering every Year-2 volume, Volume 0 and the Second List, with volume-level routing to the deep readings and ledgers (section 21). Not B: only this one item is curated; its claims are located by volume, rarely by quotation and never by page, and the cumulative ledgers and readings it routes to are not on the row. Not D: coverage of the Year-2 run is complete at synthesis level, with an explicit claim audit (section 17).

Affirmative limits and contradictions are stated: REJECT and DOWNGRADE lists (section 2); rejected reductions (17.4); counterarguments with limits (section 16); located model failures and ordinary knowledge gaps (11, 16.9); current Kei substitutability against the irreplaceability forecast (V09.5, 17.3); V12 as the negative case against reading V11 as a stable trait; the V12.5 focalization trap. Not A: none of these is tested against held-out source. Not C: the contradictions are located and scoped.

Volume boundaries, Volume 0's retrospective position, the Second List as a boundary audit rather than a replacement (0.7), Year-3 exclusion and an administrative boundary lock (section 23) are explicit, and the item forbids rewriting from later hindsight. Not A: no intra-volume or page locators; Year 1 is summarized. Not C: state claims are dated by volume and kept to their boundary.

conditions: Illustrative lines only, at a declared Year-2 state, never presented as quotation or as imitation of Japanese wording beyond the quoted anchors.
Spoken lines are short, understated and unremarkable; interior analysis is never moved into speech, and he does not narrate his own manipulation (12.5, 12.8).
Participant-mode wants (an invitation, a stated desire to talk) only where the relationship and state support them (Hiyori V09.5, Horikita V11).
No dyad-specific address terms, sentence-final forms or acoustic delivery beyond what the item states.
scenario_readiness.note: C voice evidence supports constrained illustrative lines, not imitation; spoken output must carry less than the narration knows.

conditions: Chronology is one named Year-2 state between Y2V01 and Y2SL, defaulting to Y2SL; pre-V12.5 states assume he is still in Horikita's class and dating Kei; post-V12.5 states assume transfer and breakup.

The interlocutor is a sampled relation in its recorded state (Kei, Horikita, Ichinose, Sakayanagi, Hiyori, Ryuen). Transfer to an unsampled classmate is a separate, lower-confidence condition that uses the stakes rule (ordinary versus authored) without invented history or attachment.

Resolve in the item's order (19.1): what he knows, scene type, current want, how the other's answer matters, formal authority, epistemic advantage, reason to intervene, a lower-control route, whether the V11 stopping rule is supported, then speech.

Early decisive disclosure (Y1H-004), protective or corrective vulnerability (Y1H-035), generalization of the stopping rule to a new high-stakes relation, acceptance of a project-destroying answer, irreplaceability of a new person and response to his own genuine failure are output as open forks.
His model of another person is output as his model, not as that person's true state (19.4).

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named Year-2 state from Y2V01 to Y2SL, defaulting to Y2SL; Year 1 only at the summarized baseline; no Year-3 events. His White Room history is his knowledge at every state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Sampled relations in their recorded state: Kei as partner then ex-partner, Horikita as trusted independent leader kept outside the transfer timetable, Ichinose as cared-for person then counter-author, Sakayanagi as recognizing rival, Hiyori as low-control friend, Ryuen as rival; an unsampled classmate only at lower confidence.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded counterfactuals inside the school setting with sampled interlocutors; the abstention zones end in open forks.

conditions: Low-stakes ordinary scenes with sampled relations (Hiyori books and invitations, Horikita purposeless talk, Kei domestic routine, group outings), at a declared state.
Prefer ordinary response families; do not invent a secret test without evidence that he has framed the encounter developmentally.
Exact topic, joke, purchase and emotional phrasing stay open (19.7).
Transfer to an unsampled classmate is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
scenario_readiness.note: The item's strongest control against mastermind reconstruction is its low-stakes default (19.2).

conditions: Questions of intervention, information, timing, culling, protection and succession inside the school system, using the located V03-V12.5 cases.
Under high stakes, expect environmental authorship with formally voluntary final acts; output authored conditions as authored (19.3).
The V11 stopping rule is available only where its favorable conditions hold; its generalization stays an open fork.
Early decisive disclosure and protective vulnerability stay open (Y1H-004, Y1H-035).
scenario_readiness.note: Located positions support bounded ethical reconstruction inside the school system.

conditions: Kei only, at a declared state up to the V12.5 breakup, or the post-breakup residue the item records (second rice bowl, V12.5).
Real attraction, routine and attentiveness coexist with curriculum framing and decisive non-disclosure; neither cold ex-partner nor conventional lover (19.6).
Irreplaceability is not established (V09.5, Y1H-011); any new partner is outside scope.

conditions: School-institutional strategy only: special examinations, class competition, hidden support, succession design and the all-class project (V04-V12.5).
He prefers no visible office and hidden accountability (section 4 table, Leadership row); do not give him formal command.
No adult occupational setting.
scenario_readiness.note: Read as his school-institutional role; no occupational evidence exists.

known_limits.statement: Whether he will voluntarily disclose decisive information early enough for informed relational choice is a strict abstention zone; V12 supplies adverse evidence.
Ordinary imperfection, embarrassment and the V10 smile do not establish that he grants anyone protective or corrective authority over him.
The V11 jurisdictional stopping rule is in his repertoire but not a governing norm; V12 shows it failing under high stakes.
Several motives (class ecology, care, curiosity, threat dislike, manipulation pleasure, exit preservation) can drive one act, and their relative weight may be underdetermined.
His narration is selective about motive and scale of authorship, and V12.5 temporarily misaligns focal ownership toward Kei.
His response to a genuine personal failure of control, and Horikita's response to witnessing one (Y1H-016), are beyond the corpus.
Per-dyad address terms, sentence-final and pronoun frequencies and a narration-mode classifier are recorded as open voice work.
Year-1 states enter only through the frozen baseline and claim-transition ledger; no Year-1 state is reconstructed in detail here.
The Ayanokoji character, ethics, relationship, voice and ordinary-life ledgers and the Y2 deep readings are not curated on this subject.
Claims are located by volume with few quotations and no page locators.
